universal_lens: The mapping of spatiotemporal sports dynamics to narrative constructs is formalized as a projection operator acting on high-dimensional trajectory manifolds. This unifies continuous kinematic state vectors with discrete semantic annotations, establishing a rigorous geometric framework for translating raw physical events into structured, interpretable storytelling primitives. A mathematical framework unifying data video authoring and sports analytics through structured transformation of temporal visual signals into semantically enriched narrative streams.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian filtering over the latent spatial-temporal trajectories extracted from video feeds. Conformal inference bounds are applied to player tracking uncertainties, ensuring that generated highlight clips maintain strict probabilistic guarantees regarding event relevance and tactical significance across varying camera perspectives. Bayesian inference models for probabilistic annotation of player actions and tactical patterns within video streams, enabling conformal prediction of game outcomes via latent variable modeling.
gse_mapping: GSE models gameplay as a continuous-time Markov decision process where narrative features act as reward shaping functions. The interactive timeline visualizes state transitions, allowing coaches to query counterfactual tactical outcomes by manipulating the underlying kinematic state vectors within the simulation engine. Situational reasoning engine mapping real-time video states to discrete tactical configurations using Markovian state transitions conditioned on player pose and trajectory data.

primitives.name: Spatiotemporal Narrative Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: ABSTRACT Video storytelling is essential for sports performance analysis and fan engagement, enabling sports professionals and fans to effectively communicate and interpret the spatial and temporal dynamics of gameplay.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Spatial dynamics: position vectors \mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^2 (meters). Temporal dynamics: time series t \in \mathbb{R} (seconds). Narrative: discrete semantic labels L.
primitives.assumptions: Gameplay dynamics can be accurately discretized into finite temporal windows without losing critical tactical information.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during extreme occlusions or when frame rates drop below the Nyquist frequency of rapid athletic maneuvers.

layer2.mapping: Maps continuous kinematic flows directly to discrete narrative graph nodes, preserving topological invariants of team formations.
layer2.telemetry: Narrative coherence score derived from user engagement metrics.

primitives.name: Cognitive Load Penalty
primitives.verbatim_quote: Traditional methods rely on manual annotation and verbal explanations, placing significant demands on creators for video editing skills and on viewers for cognitive focus.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Cognitive load C: dimensionless scalar [0, 1]. Manual effort E: time units (hours). Information entropy H: bits per second.
primitives.assumptions: Viewer cognitive capacity is bounded; excessive manual annotations increase perceptual noise rather than signal clarity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when audience expertise exceeds the simplified model's assumptions, requiring raw data access instead of curated narratives.

layer2.mapping: Quantifies the friction between raw telemetry ingestion and human-comprehensible output, serving as a loss function for automated editing.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in average clip production time (minutes).

primitives.name: Interactive Canvas Manifold
primitives.verbatim_quote: It combines player tracking, embedded interaction design, and timeline visualizations to seamlessly integrate narratives and visual cues within game contexts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Tracking coordinates \mathbf{p}_t \in \mathbb{R}^2 (pixels/meters). Interaction vector \mathbf{i} \in \mathbb{R}^n (dimensionless UI states).
primitives.assumptions: User interactions on the 2D canvas map bijectively to specific alterations in the underlying 3D kinematic state space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur when multiple players occupy identical pixel coordinates, causing tracking ID swaps and canvas ambiguity.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic mapping between 2D UI drag-and-drop operations and 4D spacetime clipping operations in the GSE backend.
layer2.telemetry: Interaction latency (ms) and gesture accuracy rate.

primitives.name: Empirical Adoption Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Since its launch, over 150 sports users, including coaches, athletes, content creators, parents and fans, have utilized SportsBuddy to produce compelling game highlights for diverse use cases.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: User count N = 150 (dimensionless). Use case diversity D: categorical distribution over user roles.
primitives.assumptions: Active usage correlates positively with the tool's ability to reduce the cognitive load penalty defined in primitive 2.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Metric saturation occurs if the user base grows exponentially without proportional increases in computational throughput.

layer2.mapping: Acts as a validation kernel for the GSI inference models, confirming real-world utility across heterogeneous agent types.
layer2.telemetry: Monthly active users (MAU) and highlight generation frequency.

primitives.name: Data Video Authoring Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: 2.3 Authoring Data Videos While data videos are a powerful medium for storytelling, creating them requires significant expertise in data analysis and video crafting.
primitives.assumptions: Creation of data videos assumes availability of structured data inputs and user-defined narrative templates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When data inputs lack semantic alignment with video frames, authoring fails due to misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Maps structured data to visual narrative through automated animation and synchronization logic.
layer2.telemetry: User-effort ratio during video generation and success rate of automatic transitions.

primitives.name: Augmented Sports Visualization Layer
primitives.verbatim_quote: SportsBuddy differs from these systems in two key aspects: (1) it focuses on authoring augmented sports videos with embedded data visualizations rather than general-purpose data videos; and (2) it emphasizes real-world deployment by collecting real user data to refine its usability and functionality.
primitives.assumptions: Embedded visualizations must be semantically aligned with gameplay dynamics and interpretable by viewers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When visualization overlays conflict with original video content, perceptual clarity degrades.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between raw video and enriched tactical annotations via pose estimation and tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of player tracking and overlay fidelity in real-time playback.

primitives.name: Streamlined Workflow Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: General-purpose video editing tools like Adobe Premiere Pro [1] allow users to manipulate visual elements through animation keyframing and presets, but they often involve extensive manual effort and a steep learning curve.
primitives.assumptions: Workflow efficiency increases inversely with number of manual steps required for video editing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Manual intervention exceeds threshold when user lacks domain-specific knowledge.

layer2.mapping: Reduces user effort by automating repetitive video editing tasks through guided UI and batch processing.
layer2.telemetry: Average time to complete video creation task and percentage of fully automated steps.

primitives.name: Real-Time User Feedback Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: SportsBuddy seeks to bridge the gap between academic research and industry by developing an easy-to-use tool targeted at real-world users.
primitives.assumptions: Feedback collection improves system adaptability and reduces cognitive load on users.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Feedback loop becomes ineffective when data is not representative of actual usage patterns.

layer2.mapping: Maps user behavior logs to model refinement parameters for iterative improvement of video generation quality.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of feedback submission and correlation with feature adoption rates.

primitives.name: Caption Input Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: Users can (a) input captions manually, (b) create AI-generated captions, and (c) see instant caption update in the video.
primitives.assumptions: User inputs are synchronized with video timeline at sub-second resolution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When caption length exceeds 5 seconds, automatic truncation occurs.

layer2.mapping: Caption input corresponds to a time-series signal mapping where each segment is a labeled event in the video timeline.

primitives.name: Subtitle Timeline Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Captions can be typed directly, with each line mapped to a corresponding subtitle track on the video timeline.
primitives.assumptions: Each subtitle aligns temporally with a fixed video segment duration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Alignment fails when subtitle duration exceeds video segment boundary.

layer2.mapping: Subtitle alignment kernel computes temporal overlap between caption and video frame sequence using dynamic programming.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal jitter < 50ms across all subtitle tracks

primitives.name: AI Caption Generation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Additionally, the user can select AI Captions feature to automatically generate subtitles, with options to create sentences from 1- to 5-second video segments.
primitives.assumptions: AI model outputs are conditioned on 1–5 second video clips with semantic coherence constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Generation fails when clip duration is less than 1 second or exceeds 5 seconds.

layer2.mapping: AI caption generation mirrors a conditional language model trained on video-text pairs, producing structured captions aligned with temporal segments.

primitives.name: Video Canvas Structure
primitives.verbatim_quote: The video canvas consists of a video preview (b1), an editing toolbar (b2), and a video timeline (b3): • Video Preview.
primitives.assumptions: Canvas components are spatially partitioned with defined UI interaction zones.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Canvas becomes non-functional if any component fails to render due to memory exhaustion.

layer2.mapping: Canvas structure defines a topological space where UI elements map to functional states in the editing pipeline.

primitives.name: Hybrid Design Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: To balance diverse user needs with our design goal of simplifying highlight creation for sports professionals, we designed SportsBuddy to incorporate both customization and automation.
primitives.assumptions: User preferences vary across skill levels; automation must scale without sacrificing personalization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When user expertise exceeds tool capabilities, customization becomes critical.

layer2.mapping: The hybrid kernel mirrors GSI's probabilistic decision-making framework by aligning user intent with automated action sequences.
layer2.telemetry: User engagement rate with customization features vs. default outputs.

primitives.name: Narrative Visualization Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Figure 5: SportsBuddy enhances the effectiveness and diversity of video creation for athletic communication, game analysis, and storytelling, supporting use cases such as highlighting (a) player synergy, (b) tactics, (c) spatial actions, and (d) player performance.
primitives.assumptions: Visual narratives improve comprehension of complex game dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When narrative clarity is compromised, visual fidelity degrades.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s spatial-temporal reasoning module through symbolic representation of player movement and interaction.
layer2.telemetry: Time spent viewing highlighted segments correlates with retention of tactical insights.

primitives.name: Adaptive AI Feedback Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: While this represents just one approach to AI automation in sports highlight creation, our interactive design allows users to easily refine and adjust AI-generated content.
primitives.assumptions: Human-in-the-loop refinement improves AI accuracy over repeated iterations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Feedback convergence occurs when deviation from desired output falls below threshold.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSI’s active learning paradigm where user corrections update model parameters in real time.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in post-editing time after iterative AI-assisted generation.

primitives.name: Dynamic Content Synthesis Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: This foundation is built with scalability in mind, paving the way for future AI model enhancements and fostering seamless human-AI collaboration.
primitives.assumptions: Scalability requires modular architecture supporting incremental AI upgrades.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degradation occurs at exponential growth in concurrent video streams.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSE’s distributed state machine, enabling parallel processing of video synthesis tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Throughput per second of generated highlight reels under varying load conditions.
